title: What is a Preposition?
content: A preposition is a word that shows the relationship between a noun (or pronoun) and other words in a sentence. Prepositions indicate time, place, direction, situation, or comparison.

title: Simple Prepositions
content: Simple prepositions are single words: in, on, at, by, over, under, through, between, above, below, near, along, across, behind, inside, outside, towards, since, for, during, before, after, against, around, beside, onto, within, without.

title: Prepositions of Time
content: Use 'at' for specific times (at noon, at 5pm). Use 'on' for specific days and dates (on Monday, on March 5th). Use 'in' for months, years, and parts of the day (in October, in 1995, in the morning). Use 'since' for a starting point (since 5pm). Use 'for' for a duration (for an hour).

title: Prepositions of Place
content: Use 'at' for a specific point or location (at the station, at home). Use 'in' for an enclosed space or area (in the box, in the room). Use 'on' for surfaces (on the table, on the wall). Other place prepositions include: above, below, behind, beside, between, under, over, near, inside, outside, across, along.

title: What are Prepositional Phrases?
content: A prepositional phrase = preposition + article/determiner + noun. Examples: 'in the house', 'on the table', 'under the bridge', 'after the movie', 'during the game'. They function as adjectives or adverbs in sentences: 'After the movie, we went home.' / 'The cat sleeps on the couch.'

title: Compound Prepositions
content: Compound prepositions are made of two or more words: according to, instead of, apart from, due to, because of, on behalf of, in front of, on top of, out of, away from, next to, in spite of, regardless of, by means of, with respect to, in line with, as far as, in order to, prior to, as well as.

title: Fixed Prepositional Phrases
content: Some prepositional phrases are fixed expressions: 'on time' (punctual), 'on holiday/vacation', 'on strike', 'on a diet', 'on purpose', 'on behalf of', 'in favor of', 'in debt', 'in danger', 'in love', 'in a hurry', 'by accident', 'by heart', 'by chance', 'at home', 'at your service', 'under construction', 'under control'.

title: Quiz: Compound Preposition Usage
question_text: Which sentence uses the preposition correctly?
options: She arrived according to the schedule.
She arrived according with the schedule.
She arrived according from the schedule.

explanation: 'According to' is the correct compound preposition. It always requires 'to' after it.
